_doc: Wire schema for sleuth_mcp tool-call return shapes. Sidecar-only — the root sleuth package does not ship a parallel copy. Audit source: packages/sleuth_mcp/test/schema/mcp_tool_schema_audit_test.dart. Human-readable render at mcp_tool_schema.md.
notes: Error envelopes describe current sidecar handler behavior — each handler returns ToolCallResult.text(...) with `isError: true` and a single text content carrying the message string. Codes listed in `errors[].code` appear verbatim as the prefix of that text. A centralized typed error class is acknowledged debt.

Passthrough tools delegate to bridge.callExtension and return the ext.sleuth.* envelope unmodified. Documented shims (get_route_health v0.32 -> v0.33 wrapper, get_issues severityAtLeast filter, compact-issue projection on get_issues + get_snapshot) are spelled out explicitly so the audit can assert the shim's behavior.
Snapshot / route-session nested shapes live in mcp_schema.{json,md}. This file documents only the tool-layer wrapping.

schemaVersion 2 adds the compact-issue projection: get_issues and get_snapshot trim each issue to the actionable subset by default (severity, category, confidence, title, detail, fixHint, stableId, widgetName, routeName, sourceRoute, confidenceReason, rootCauseIds). Pass verbose:true for the full ~22-field shape. Compaction is field-only and lossless for the diff key (stableId + severity), so compare_snapshots and check_budgets work on compact snapshots.

Transport (cross-cutting, not a per-tool shape): for clients that negotiate MCP protocol >= 2025-06-18, every SUCCESS tools/call result also carries a top-level `structuredContent` field — the same JSON the text content block carries, as an object. Clients on older protocol versions see the text content only. structuredContent is never set on error results (isError:true). This is additive and does not change any per-tool data/args/errors shape below, so schemaVersion stays 2.

toolAnnotations locks the three non-readOnly MCP annotation hints (destructiveHint, idempotentHint, openWorldHint) per tool; readOnlyHint stays sourced from readOnlyTools (not duplicated here). Only non-default hints are listed. openWorldHint:true for tools whose output reflects external/runtime state (the live-app readers get_snapshot/get_issues/get_route_health/diagnose/check_budgets and the host enumerator list_devices); false for self-contained tools (explain_issue static content, compare_snapshots local diff, app_status server-internal status). destructiveHint:true for detach_app (it terminates the session and deletes disk-handoff files); destructive/idempotent are omitted on read-only tools (the spec ignores those unless readOnlyHint is false). Annotations are advisory descriptor metadata, not a tool return/args shape, so schemaVersion stays 2.

The audit enforces descriptor<->toolAnnotations CONSISTENCY, not value-vs-behavior CORRECTNESS — a hint that disagrees with what a handler actually does (e.g. a destructive tool marked non-destructive) passes as long as the descriptor and this doc agree. Hint values are a spec/behavior judgment, reviewed against the MCP ToolAnnotations spec + the handlers, not machine-verified.

data._doc: Passes through ext.sleuth.diagnose.data and augments with two sidecar-stamped keys. All ext.sleuth.diagnose keys remain present.

launchModeAdvisory.presence: when connectionMode is warmup/disconnected, or basic without a live VM self-connect (vmConnected false) — VM-only detectors degraded; nudges a --no-dds relaunch

sections.doc: Subset of payload sections; forwarded to ext.sleuth.snapshot as a comma-joined string. Omit for full payload.

maxIssueCount.doc: Keep top-N already-ranked issues (lib-side cap on currentIssues).

maxRouteCount.doc: Keep N most-recent routes by startedAt.

diskHandoff.doc: When true, write the envelope to a temp file; the tool returns {path, sizeBytes, sha256, _projectedSections?, _projectionLimits?, _projectionApplied?} instead of inline data.

verbose.doc: When false (default) each data.currentIssues entry is trimmed to the compact actionable subset; true returns full issue fields. Field shape only — independent of the maxIssueCount cap, which is applied lib-side regardless.

shims.name: compact_issues
shims.doc: Unless verbose:true, the sidecar trims every data.currentIssues entry to the compact key set (severity, category, confidence, title, detail, fixHint, stableId, widgetName, routeName, sourceRoute, confidenceReason, rootCauseIds), copying only keys that are present. Runs on both the inline-return and disk-handoff paths from a fresh map (bridge envelope never mutated). No-op when currentIssues was projected out via `sections` or is absent/non-list. Lossless for stableId + severity, so compare_snapshots / check_budgets still operate on compact snapshots.

shims.name: disk_handoff
shims.doc: When `diskHandoff` is true the sidecar serializes the snapshot envelope to a per-process Directory.systemTemp/sleuth_snapshot_<pid>/<random>.json file (128-bit Random.secure name). The per-pid dir is created 0700 and the file 0600, both verified via FileStat; if owner-only perms cannot be set+verified on POSIX the file is deleted and a `disk_handoff_failed` error is returned (fail-closed). On Windows POSIX modes don't apply. The payload MAY contain mildly-sensitive data (e.g. recentRequests[].url with query tokens), hence the fail-closed perms. Returns {path, sizeBytes, sha256} plus any projection metadata, rather than the inline `data` block. Files are deleted on detach_app, on sidecar shutdown, and aged files (30 min) in the process's own dir are swept on each new write (per-pid dir prevents cross-instance sweeps). When `diskHandoff` is false/absent the envelope passes through unmodified. Lineage fallback: if the app predates projection support and a projection arg was requested, the sidecar stamps `_projectionApplied: by_sidecar_fallback` on the disk-handoff path; on the inline path it returns `projection_unsupported_by_app` instead (the full payload would overflow the response cap).

data._doc: Passthrough of ext.sleuth.snapshot.data; the sidecar adds launchModeAdvisory on a degraded session.

launchModeAdvisory.presence: stamped in data on a degraded session (connectionMode warmup/disconnected, or basic without a live VM self-connect); warns the snapshot is incomplete (VM-only detectors suppressed). Rides in the written file on the disk-handoff path.

maxIssueCount.doc: Keep the front-N of the app's already-ranked order (post severity filter). 0 means unbounded; negative is rejected with arg_invalid_int. Applies whether or not verbose is set.

verbose.doc: When false (default) each kept issue in data.issues is trimmed to the compact actionable subset; true returns full issue fields. Field shape only — the maxIssueCount cap still applies.

data._doc: Passthrough of ext.sleuth.issues, then field-trimmed + capped. data.issues entries carry the compact key set unless verbose:true. The two keys below are stamped on data only when the cap dropped at least one issue.

_truncated.presence: stamped true only when maxIssueCount dropped at least one issue from data.issues

_totalCount.presence: post-filter pre-cap issue count; stamped alongside _truncated

severityAtLeast.presence: echo stamped only when the severity filter was applied

launchModeAdvisory.presence: stamped in data on a degraded session (connectionMode warmup/disconnected, or basic without a live VM self-connect); warns the issue list is incomplete (VM-only detectors suppressed)

shims.name: severity_filter
shims.doc: When `severityAtLeast` is `warning` or `critical`, the sidecar filters `data.issues` to entries whose severity meets the threshold AND adds `data.severityAtLeast` echoing the requested level. When `severityAtLeast` is `ok` or absent, no filter + no echo.

shims.name: compact_projection
shims.doc: After the optional severity filter, data.issues is capped to the front maxIssueCount entries (default 50; 0 = unbounded) of the app's already-ranked order, then — unless verbose:true — each kept entry is trimmed to compactIssueKeys (only present keys copied). When the cap dropped any issue, data gains `_truncated:true` + `_totalCount` (post-filter pre-cap count). Error envelopes (no `data` map / no `issues` list) pass through unmodified.

errors.doc: maxIssueCount is negative (or non-integer); only 0 disables the cap
ext.sleuth.issues returned an error envelope — passed through unmodified

shims.name: lineage_route_wrapper
shims.doc: When the `route` arg is provided and the bridge is connected to an `acceptedPriorLineages` app emitting the v0.32 inline RouteSession shape (data carries `routeName` but no `route` key), the shim wraps data into `{route: <inline-session>}` so downstream consumers always see the canonical v0.33 envelope. v0.33+ apps already emit the wrapper and pass through untouched. Error envelopes and absent-route shapes are never wrapped.
